```python

```

should write the full prompt text `"Prompt to stderr with no suffix"` cleanly to stderr with nothing leaking to stdout, but currently part of the text is misplaced. Fix prompt readline features on non-Windows platforms

On non-Windows platforms, click.prompt() and click.confirm() were
splitting the prompt text across multiple calls - printing all but the
last character via echo(), then passing only the last character to the
input function. This broke readline features like backspace and
line-wrapping. Additionally, when err=True and/or prompt_suffix="" was
used, output was split incorrectly between stdout and stderr.

The fix passes the full prompt directly to the input function on

for colorama compatibility. For visible prompts with err=True, the
prompt is now written to stderr first, then input() is called with an
empty prompt. For hidden input, the full prompt is passed to
getpass.getpass() which naturally uses stderr.

This ensures readline works correctly and output is not split between
streams.
EOF
)"
